walkthroughs.body_html:
World Focus Music Study — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World Focus Music Study brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with World Focus Music Study.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: It is the same as the chorus.
Three notes played at once.
It is the very first section.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.
Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together.
It is the very first section.
A single melody with chord accompaniment.
Loud music with many instruments.
Three notes played at once.
It is the very first section.
Vibrato on a single note.
Rapid alternation between the written note and the note a step above.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Riff”?
options: Chord progression I-IV-V over 12 bars; underpins blues, rock and roll.
Common pop structure alternating verses and a memorable repeated chorus.
Reusing a portion of a sound recording in a new track, central to hip-hop.
Short, repeated melodic or rhythmic idea, common in rock and jazz.
